unit.title: Harness engineering fundamentals
unit.moc: agent = model + harness — eight components — harness beats model — failure statistics — the tribunal's map — sensors proven

checkpoint.title: Checkpoint 2 — gate
checkpoint.prompt: Classify a fictional system against the eight harness components and say which layer the tribunal itself was weakest in.

facts.text: Agent = Model + Harness. The model reasons; the harness is everything around it: what it sees, what it can do, how it recovers. Distinct from prompt engineering and model selection.

options: everything around the model — what it sees, what it can do, how it recovers

exercises.prompt: Type the formula you just heard.

facts.text: The standard harness inventory: guides (feedforward: AGENTS.md, conventions) · sensors (feedback: linters, LLM-as-judge) · memory/state · tool-execution layer · guardrails (policy) · loop controller · verification layer · failure handler / escalation.

exercises.prompt: Match each component to its role.
Which component is the FEEDFORWARD layer?
The eight components: guides, sensors, ___, tool-execution, guardrails, loop controller, ___, failure handler.

facts.text: Evidence cited in the literature: harness changes outperform model changes (5–14 benchmark points, −20% tokens, same model); Manus rewrote its harness 5x in 6 months with the same model.

options: 5–14 benchmark points and −20% tokens on the same model

exercises.prompt: Manus rewrote its harness ___ in 6 months with the same model.
The moral of this lesson is:
options: improve the harness around the model

facts.text: ~88% of agent projects never reach production; ~27% of failures trace to data quality; weak verification is the most-skipped layer (“models say done when they're not done”; non-empty output is a trivial check).

exercises.prompt: About what share of agent projects never reach production?

facts.text: The tribunal's map: Memory/state is Strong (files-only, proven clean-session bootstrap); Guardrails are Strong (structural: DeepSeek-once, secret→oc-qw, MAX_LANES=4); Sensors are Weak (byte counts = the “trivial check” the literature warns about); Verification is “doctrine, not machinery” — the most-skipped layer.

exercises.prompt: Which layers of the tribunal are STRONGEST?
The tribunal's sensors are weak because:
options: byte count is the “trivial check” the literature warns about
there are too many of them
they run on the wrong lane

exercises.prompt: The tribunal's verification was described as:

facts.text: Two live defects proved the sensor gap: (1) `class: lane-benchmark` auto-picked 5 lanes, failing MAX_LANES=4 AND violating the DeepSeek-once guard; (2) `hub verdict` used substring match, so a slug that is a substring of another rewrote the wrong ledger row.

options: 5 lanes were auto-picked, failing MAX_LANES=4 and DeepSeek-once
substring match could rewrite the wrong ledger row

exercises.prompt: Why do these matter as a lesson?
options: both are exactly the sensor gap they prove
